title: Coq au Vin
subtitle: French chicken braised in red wine with lardons and mushrooms
excerpt: The great French farmhouse braise: chicken joints slow-cooked in a full bottle of Burgundy with lardons, pearl onions, mushrooms, and a bouquet garni until the wine reduces to a glossy, winey, deeply savoury sauce. Julia Child's version remains definitive.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coq au vin (literally 'rooster in wine') is a classic French braise from the Burgundy region, historically made with old rooster (which required a long wine braise to tenderise), now typically made with chicken. It appears in French culinary canon as early as the Roman era, though the modern recipe was codified in twentieth century French cookery and popularised internationally by Julia Child's 'Mastering the Art of French Cooking' (1961). The dish is built on the principle of cooking the chicken gently in enough wine (classically a whole bottle of Burgundy) to surround and penetrate the joints, with lardons for fat and saltiness, mushrooms for earthiness, and pearl onions for sweetness. The sauce reduction and enrichment at the end is the distinguishing step between a good and exceptional coq au vin.

content.text: Marinating the chicken in the wine overnight is optional but deepens the flavour considerably. Brown the lardons and chicken separately and thoroughly. The sauce should reduce significantly before serving; a flat, watery sauce means insufficient reduction. Finish with a tablespoon of butter stirred off the heat for richness.

items.preparation: a full bottle of Burgundy or other Pinot Noir
small; peeled and left whole; or pearl onions

content.text: Fry the lardons in the oil in a large casserole until crispy. Remove. Brown the seasoned chicken joints on all sides in the rendered fat until deeply golden. Remove. Cook the shallots until coloured. Add the garlic and tomato puree for 1 minute.
Return the lardons and chicken. Pour in the wine and stock. Add the bay and thyme. Bring to a very gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 1 hour until the chicken is tender. Remove the chicken.

Fry the mushrooms separately in butter until golden. Add to the sauce. Boil the sauce uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes until reduced and glossy. Return the chicken to reheat. Swirl in the butter off the heat. Taste and season. Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread.
